evals.name: basic-tiled-ensemble-run
evals.prompt: How do I run the tiled ensemble pipeline to train Padim on MVTecAD bottle with 128x128 tiles?
evals.expected_output: Run python tools/tiled_ensemble/train.py --config ens_config.yaml with tiling.tile_size=[128,128] and TrainModels.model.class_path=Padim in the config.
expectations: Sets tiling.tile_size to [128, 128] in the YAML config
Configures data.class_path to anomalib.data.MVTecAD with category bottle

evals.name: config-structure
evals.prompt: Show me the YAML config structure for the tiled ensemble pipeline with overlapping tiles and seam smoothing enabled.
evals.expected_output: Config with tiling.stride < tiling.tile_size for overlap, SeamSmoothing.apply=True with sigma and width parameters.
expectations: Shows tiling section with image_size, tile_size, and stride
Sets stride less than tile_size to create overlap
Includes SeamSmoothing section with apply: True
Shows sigma and width parameters for seam smoothing

evals.name: eval-pipeline
evals.prompt: I've trained a tiled ensemble. How do I run evaluation on it?
evals.expected_output: Run python tools/tiled_ensemble/eval.py --config ens_config.yaml --root results/Padim/MVTecAD/bottle/v0 pointing at the training output directory.
expectations: Passes --root pointing to the training run's output directory
Uses the same config file as the training run

evals.name: cost-awareness
evals.prompt: I want to use 64x64 tiles with stride 32 on 512x512 images. Any concerns?
evals.expected_output: Warns that the pipeline trains one model per tile position, so many tiles = high cost. With 512/32 stride = 16x16 = 256 tile positions, each getting its own model instance.
expectations: Warns that one model is trained per tile position (not shared)
Calculates or mentions the tile count grows with smaller stride
Advises budgeting compute cost before scaling up tile configurations

evals.name: negative-single-model-redirect
evals.prompt: I just want to train a single Padim model on MVTecAD normally without any tiling. Should I use the tiled ensemble?
evals.expected_output: No — for single-model training, use the standard Engine.fit() flow (see anomalib-training skill). Tiled ensemble is for high-resolution scenarios needing per-tile models.
expectations: Redirects to standard Engine.fit() training flow
Does not suggest using tiled ensemble for simple single-model training
Explains tiled ensemble is specifically for high-resolution multi-tile scenarios
